overview: Uganda is a landlocked country in East Africa. Its capital and largest city is Kampala. Uganda became independent from the United Kingdom in 1962. English and Swahili are official languages, and the country is home to many ethnic groups. Winston Churchill called it the 'Pearl of Africa'.

geography.text: Uganda sits on a high plateau and includes a large part of Lake Victoria, the largest lake in Africa, from which the Nile begins its long journey north. The Rwenzori Mountains, sometimes called the 'Mountains of the Moon', rise along the western border, and its forests are home to mountain gorillas and chimpanzees.

history.text: The Kingdom of Buganda was the most powerful of several kingdoms around Lake Victoria. Britain made Uganda a protectorate in 1894, and it became independent in 1962. Idi Amin seized power in 1971 and ruled brutally until 1979, when Tanzanian troops and Ugandan exiles overthrew him. Yoweri Museveni has led the country since 1986.

events.title: Speke reaches the Nile's source
events.text: John Hanning Speke reaches Lake Victoria's outflow.

events.title: Asians expelled
events.text: Idi Amin expels Uganda's Asian community.

events.title: Amin overthrown
events.text: Tanzanian forces help remove Idi Amin.

government.text: Uganda is a presidential republic. Yoweri Museveni has been President since 1986; presidential term and age limits were removed. Opposition supporters often face arrests.

economy.text: Uganda exports coffee, gold, fish and tea. Oil fields near Lake Albert are being developed with a pipeline to Tanzania.

culture.text: Uganda is called the 'Pearl of Africa'. Lake Victoria, Africa's largest lake, and the source of the White Nile are there. Bark cloth, made from fig trees, is listed by UNESCO, and Uganda is home to about half of the world's mountain gorillas.

items.title: Source of the Nile
items.text: The White Nile flows out of Lake Victoria at Jinja.

items.title: Bwindi
items.text: Impenetrable forest home to mountain gorillas.

sport.text: Athletics and football are popular. Joshua Cheptegei holds the 5,000 m and 10,000 m world records and won Olympic gold in 2021 and 2024. Peruth Chemutai won the steeplechase in 2021.
